newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 11.0/12.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 11.0/12.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 11.0/12.0 percent from 15.0/16.0 percent on Thursday morning.
Dealers said initial high overnight rates resulted from a slump in overnight rates late on Wednesday which led operators to park their excess funds in one-week bilateral papers (SBIs).
"This seemed to cause some shortages this morning and pushed overnight rates to rise," one local bank dealer said.
She said, however, initial worries were unfounded because overall liquidity demand was relatively small.
Short-dated swap rates fell following softening of short-term money. Overnight swaps fell to 1.75 from 2.2 points.

The central bank offered one-to-three day SBIs at five percent, one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.75 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 10.26 percent, compared with 11.47 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said the secondary market had quietened down due to a slew of new issues in the primary market.
"The market is a bit soft. We focus on new issues at present," one bond dealer said.
